images.caption: Figure 1:Teaser.We presentGRACE, a novel latent compression technique that fine-tunes pretrained video generation models, such as Wan2.1-14B(Wan et al., 2025), to generate from substantially fewer latent tokens (e.g., nearly𝟖×8\timesfewer).(Top)Text-to-video (T2V) samples at 736p from Wan2.1-14B before compression and from GRACE, using the same prompt.(Bottom left)The same comparison at 480p.(Bottom right)On VBench-T2V(Huang et al., 2023;Huang et al., 2024), GRACE preserves the generation quality of Wan2.1-14B before compression and achieves higher scores than existing high-compression autoencoders(HaCohen et al., 2024;Zheng et al., 2026;He et al., 2026), while generating11.1×11.1\timesfaster at 480p and15.5×15.5\timesfaster at 736p. All models in the plot are evaluated at matched resolutions with 50 sampling steps. The plot reports text-to-video, and the speedups above are measured on image-to-video.

Figure 2:Overall architecture.Stage 1 trains the autoencoder. The frozen encoderℰ\mathcal{E}maps the downsampled input to𝐳base\mathbf{z}_{\text{base}}, the residual encoderℰres\mathcal{E}_{\text{res}}maps the full-resolution input to𝐳res\mathbf{z}_{\text{res}}, and𝒟^\hat{\mathcal{D}}decodes both, whileℒalign\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}matches the compressed latent to the pretrained latent inside the frozen DiT. The dashed box on the right of Stage 1 shows a simplified view of the blocks added toℰres\mathcal{E}_{\text{res}}and𝒟^\hat{\mathcal{D}}. Stage 2 adapts the DiT to the compressed latent with LoRA, denoising𝐳base\mathbf{z}_{\text{base}}at a lower noise level than𝐳res\mathbf{z}_{\text{res}}at every step, so the base is denoised first.
